facts.text: You must have a CDL to drive any single vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating of 26,001 pounds or more.
You must have a CDL to drive a combination vehicle with a gross combination weight rating of 26,001 pounds or more, when the vehicle being towed is rated over 10,000 pounds.
You must have a CDL to drive a vehicle designed to carry 16 or more passengers, including the driver.
You must have a CDL to drive any size vehicle that needs hazardous material placards, or that carries a material listed as a select agent or toxin.
Class A is a combination of vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more, when the towed vehicle or vehicles are rated over 10,000 pounds.
Class B is a single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, or such a vehicle towing another vehicle rated at 10,000 pounds or less.
Class C is a single vehicle under 26,001 pounds GVWR, included in the CDL programme only when it carries 16 or more passengers including the driver, or needs hazmat placards.
A Class A licence also lets you drive Class B and Class C vehicles, and a Class B licence also lets you drive Class C vehicles.
There are six kinds of CDL endorsement: double and triple trailers (T), tank vehicle (N), passenger (P), hazardous materials (H), school bus (S), and the combination of tank and hazmat (X).
Only three endorsements can be added to a commercial learner's permit: passenger (P), school bus (S) and tank vehicle (N).
A tank vehicle endorsement is needed for a tank with an individual rated capacity over 119 gallons and a total rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more.

cards.q: What single vehicle weight rating needs a CDL?
cards.a: A GVWR of 26,001 lb or more.

cards.q: What combination weight ratings need a CDL?
cards.a: A GCWR of 26,001 lb or more, with the towed vehicle rated over 10,000 lb.

cards.q: How many passengers make a vehicle a CDL vehicle?
cards.a: 16 or more, including the driver.

cards.q: Define a Class A vehicle.
cards.a: A combination with a GCWR of 26,001 lb or more, towing a unit rated over 10,000 lb.

cards.q: Define a Class B vehicle.
cards.a: A single vehicle of 26,001 lb GVWR or more, or one towing a unit rated 10,000 lb or less.

cards.q: Define a Class C vehicle.
cards.a: A vehicle under 26,001 lb that carries 16+ people including the driver, or needs hazmat placards.

cards.q: Which classes may a Class A holder drive?
cards.a: Class A, B and C.

cards.q: Which endorsements can go on a commercial learner's permit?
cards.a: Passenger (P), school bus (S) and tank vehicle (N) only.

cards.q: What tank capacity needs the N endorsement?
cards.a: An individual tank over 119 gallons, with 1,000 gallons or more in total.

exam.q: Which combination needs a Class A licence?
choices: A GCWR of 26,001 lb with a 12,000 lb trailer
A GCWR of 24,000 lb with a 12,000 lb trailer
A GCWR of 30,000 lb with an 8,000 lb trailer
A single truck of 30,000 lb GVWR
exam.why: Class A needs a GCWR of 26,001 lb or more AND a towed unit rated over 10,000 lb.

exam.q: A 15-passenger van weighing 9,000 lb needs which licence?
choices: No CDL for the passenger count alone
exam.why: A CDL is needed at 16 or more people including the driver, so 15 is below the limit.

reading.p: Federal law makes every state set minimum standards for licensing commercial drivers. This manual gives you the testing information. It does not give you every federal and state rule you must meet before you drive a commercial motor vehicle.

reading.h: When you must have a CDL

ul: Any single vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating of 26,001 pounds or more.
A combination vehicle with a gross combination weight rating of 26,001 pounds or more, when the vehicle being towed is rated over 10,000 pounds.
A vehicle designed to carry 16 or more passengers, including the driver.
Any size vehicle that needs hazardous material placards, or that carries a material listed as a select agent or toxin.

numbers.what: a combination: GCWR 26,001 lb or more, towed unit over 10,000 lb
a single vehicle of 26,001 lb GVWR or more, or one towing 10,000 lb or less
under 26,001 lb, but carrying 16+ people or placarded hazmat

reading.p: A Class A licence also lets you drive Class B and Class C vehicles. A Class B licence also lets you drive Class C vehicles. Driving a Class A vehicle takes a good deal more skill and knowledge than the other two.
There are six kinds of endorsement: double and triple trailers (T), tank vehicle (N), passenger (P), hazardous materials (H), school bus (S), and the tank and hazmat combination (X).

reading.note: Only three endorsements can go on a commercial learner's permit: passenger (P), school bus (S) and tank vehicle (N).

reading.p: A tank endorsement is needed for a tank with an individual rated capacity over 119 gallons and a total rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more. A hazmat endorsement needs entry level driver training and a Transportation Security Administration background check.

facts.text: The general knowledge test is taken by every CDL applicant.
You must take the air brakes test if your vehicle has air brakes, and air over hydraulic brakes count as air brakes.
The combination vehicles test is required if you want to drive combination vehicles, which includes every Class A driver.
The hazardous materials test needs entry level driver training and a Transportation Security Administration background check.
For a Class A licence the manual says to study sections 1, 2, 3, 6, 11, 12 and 13, and section 5 as well if you will drive a vehicle with air brakes.

cards.q: Which knowledge test does every CDL applicant take?
cards.a: The general knowledge test.

cards.q: Do air over hydraulic brakes count as air brakes for the test?
cards.a: Yes. You must take the air brakes test.

cards.q: Which knowledge tests does a Class A driver with air brakes take?
cards.a: General knowledge, combination vehicles, and air brakes.

cards.q: Which manual sections should a Class A applicant with air brakes study?

exam.q: Your tractor has air over hydraulic brakes. Which test must you take?
exam.why: Air over hydraulic brakes count as air brakes, so the air brakes test is required.

reading.p: How many knowledge tests you take depends on the licence class and the endorsements you want.

ul: General knowledge: every applicant takes it.
Air brakes: you must take it if your vehicle has air brakes. Air over hydraulic brakes count as air brakes.
Combination vehicles: required to drive combination vehicles, so every Class A driver takes it.
Passenger transport: every bus driver applicant.
Hazardous materials, tank vehicle, doubles and triples, and school bus: each for its own endorsement.

reading.h: What a Class A applicant studies

reading.p: Figure 1.2 in the manual lists the sections for each licence class. For Class A it names sections 1, 2, 3, 6, 11, 12 and 13, and section 5 as well if you will drive a vehicle with air brakes.

reading.note: That is the plan this app follows. Sections 4, 7, 8, 9 and 10 are endorsement material.

facts.text: The skills test has three parts: vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, and on-road driving.
You must take the three skills test parts in order, and you must pass each part before you go on to the next.
You must take the skills test in the type of vehicle you want to be licensed for.
A vehicle with marked or labelled components cannot be used for the CDL skills test.
In the vehicle inspection test you must point to or touch each item, name it, and tell the examiner what you would inspect and why.
In the basic vehicle control test you move the vehicle forward, backward and turn it inside a marked area, and the examiner tells you how each exercise is done.
You can take the skills test after you pass the required knowledge tests and finish entry level driver training.

cards.q: What are the three parts of the CDL skills test, in order?
cards.a: Vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, then on-road driving.

cards.q: Can you take the skills test parts in any order?
cards.a: No. They are taken in order, and each must be passed before the next.

cards.q: Which vehicle must you use for the skills test?
cards.a: The type of vehicle you want the licence for.

cards.q: Can a vehicle with labelled parts be used for the skills test?
cards.a: No. Marked or labelled components are not allowed.

cards.q: What must you do for each item in the vehicle inspection test?
cards.a: Point to or touch it, name it, and say what you inspect and why.

exam.q: You fail the basic vehicle control part. What happens next?
choices: You go on to the on-road test
You cannot go on to the on-road test
You get the licence with a restriction
exam.why: Each part must be passed before the next one, so a failed part stops the test there.

exam.q: During the inspection test, what must you do at each item?
choices: Point to or touch it, name it, and explain what and why
exam.why: The test needs you to point to or touch the item, name it, and explain the check.

reading.p: Once you pass the knowledge tests you need, and you finish entry level driver training, you can take the skills test when you are eligible.

ul: Vehicle inspection.
Basic vehicle control.
On-road driving.

reading.note: You take the parts in that order, and you must pass each one before you move to the next.

reading.h: What each part asks of you

ul: Vehicle inspection: you show that you know whether the vehicle is safe to drive. You must point to or touch each item, name it, and tell the examiner what you would inspect and why.
Basic vehicle control: you move the vehicle forward, backward and turn it inside a marked area. The examiner tells you how each exercise is done.
On-road driving: you drive in traffic, which can include turns, intersections, railroad crossings, curves, grades, and single or multi-lane roads. The examiner tells you where to drive.

reading.note: Take the test in the type of vehicle you want to be licensed for. A vehicle with marked or labelled components cannot be used.

facts.text: Utah requires at least one year of experience as a licensed driver before you can apply for a CDL.
Utah requires your driver licence and your current Medical Examiner's Certificate, form MCSA-5876, also called the medical certificate or DOT card.
You must give up your driver licence to the Division when you get your Utah commercial driver instruction permit, and the permit then lets you drive your own vehicle.
A CDL applicant under 21 years of age cannot get the passenger, school bus or hazardous materials endorsements.

cards.q: How much driving experience does Utah require before a CDL?
cards.a: At least one year as a licensed driver.

cards.q: Which medical form must a Utah CDL applicant provide?
cards.a: The current Medical Examiner's Certificate, MCSA-5876 (the DOT card).

cards.q: What happens to your driver licence when you get a CDIP in Utah?
cards.a: You surrender it to the Division, and the CDIP lets you drive your own vehicle.

cards.q: Which endorsements are barred under age 21 in Utah?
cards.a: Passenger, school bus and hazardous materials.

exam.q: A 20-year-old Utah applicant may NOT get which endorsement?
exam.why: Under 21, the passenger, school bus and hazmat endorsements are not available.

reading.p: Utah adds its own requirements on top of the federal ones.

ul: Your driver licence.
At least one year of experience as a licensed driver.
Your current Medical Examiner's Certificate, form MCSA-5876, also called the medical certificate or DOT card.

reading.note: You must surrender your driver licence, from Utah or another state, to the Division when you get your Utah commercial driver instruction permit. The permit then lets you drive your own vehicle.

reading.p: An applicant under 21 years of age cannot get the passenger, school bus or hazardous materials endorsements.

facts.text: You must tell the Driver License Division what type of commercial driving you do, and that is called self-certification.
If you must hold a certified medical status and you let your medical examiner's certificate lapse, you become not-certified and you can lose your CDL.

cards.q: What is self-certification?
cards.a: Telling the Division which type of commercial driving you do.

cards.q: What happens if your medical certificate lapses?
cards.a: You become not-certified and can lose your CDL.

reading.p: You must tell the state what kind of commercial driving you do. That is called self-certification, and it decides whether you must file a medical certificate.

If you apply for a CDL permit, renew, upgrade, add an endorsement or transfer from another state, you must give the state your type of commercial motor vehicle operation. Drivers in some types of commerce must also file a current medical examiner's certificate, and any medical variance papers such as a vision, skills performance or diabetic waiver.

reading.note: If you must hold a certified medical status and you let your certificate lapse, you become not-certified. You can lose your CDL, or it can be denied for not downgrading in time.

facts.text: Interstate commerce is driving a CMV from one state to another state or a foreign country.
Driving between two places inside one state is still interstate commerce if the trip crosses into another state or a foreign country during part of it.
Driving between two places inside one state is still interstate commerce if the cargo or the passengers are part of a trip that began or will end in another state or a foreign country.
Intrastate commerce is driving a CMV inside one state, and meeting none of the interstate descriptions.
If you drive in both interstate and intrastate commerce, you must choose interstate commerce.

cards.q: Define interstate commerce.
cards.a: Driving a CMV across a state or national line, or carrying cargo or people on a trip that does.

cards.q: Is a trip inside one state ever interstate commerce?
cards.a: Yes. If the trip crosses a state line, or the cargo or passengers began or will end out of state.

cards.q: You drive both interstate and intrastate. Which do you certify?
cards.a: Interstate commerce.

exam.q: You haul a load from Salt Lake City to Provo, but the load started in Nevada. What kind of commerce is it?
exam.why: Cargo on a trip that began in another state makes it interstate commerce, even inside one state.

reading.p: The first question is simple: do you cross a state line, in any sense?

ul: You drive from one state to another state or a foreign country.
You drive between two places inside one state, but part of the trip crosses into another state or a foreign country.
You drive between two places inside one state, but the cargo or the passengers are part of a trip that began, or will end, in another state or a foreign country.

reading.p: You drive inside one state and none of the three descriptions above fits.

reading.note: If you do both, you must choose interstate commerce.

subsections.title: Inter/Intrastate Commerce: Status Non-excepted or Excepted?

facts.text: A non-excepted interstate driver must give a current medical examiner's certificate to the state driver licence agency.
Most CDL holders who drive in interstate commerce are non-excepted interstate drivers.
An excepted interstate driver does not need a federal medical examiner's certificate.
If you drive in both excepted and non-excepted interstate commerce, you must choose non-excepted interstate commerce.
In Utah you are an excepted intrastate driver if you are under 21 and may drive a CMV only inside the state, and you then need a K restriction on the licence.
Excepted activities include carrying school children and staff between home and school, government work, carrying human remains or sick or injured people, and emergency fire or rescue driving.

cards.q: Which interstate status must give a medical certificate to the state?
cards.a: Non-excepted interstate.

cards.q: Which status do most interstate CDL holders have?
cards.a: Non-excepted interstate.

cards.q: You drive both excepted and non-excepted interstate. Which do you pick?
cards.a: Non-excepted interstate.

cards.q: When is a Utah driver excepted intrastate?
cards.a: Under 21 and allowed to drive a CMV only inside Utah, with a K restriction.

exam.q: Which self-certification requires you to hand a medical examiner's certificate to the state?
exam.why: Non-excepted interstate drivers must provide and keep a current MEC.

reading.p: Once you know interstate or intrastate, you choose excepted or non-excepted. That gives you one of four types of commerce to certify to.

ul: Excepted interstate: you drive in interstate commerce only for certain listed activities, and you do not need a federal medical examiner's certificate.
Non-excepted interstate: anything else. You must give a current medical examiner's certificate to the state.

reading.note: Most CDL holders who drive in interstate commerce are non-excepted interstate drivers. If you do both, choose non-excepted.

ul: Carrying school children and school staff between home and school.
Work as a federal, state or local government employee.
Carrying human remains, or sick or injured people.
Fire truck or rescue vehicle driving in an emergency.
Custom harvesting, beekeeping, or a farmer's own non-combination vehicle within 150 air miles of the farm.
Carrying migrant workers, or passengers privately for non-business purposes.

reading.p: You are an excepted intrastate driver in Utah if you are under 21 and may drive a commercial motor vehicle only inside the state. You must still meet the federal or state medical requirements, file the certificate, and carry a K restriction. On your 21st birthday you must certify under a different category.

facts.text: The L restriction means you may not drive a commercial vehicle with air brakes.
The Z restriction means you may not drive a commercial vehicle with air brakes that are not fully equipped.
The E restriction means you may not drive a commercial motor vehicle with a manual transmission.
The O restriction means you may not drive a commercial motor vehicle with a tractor-trailer.
The K restriction limits you to driving commercial vehicles inside the state only.
To remove an E, L or O restriction you must get a qualifying permit and pass the skills tests again.
Utah does not permit modified skills tests.
The B restriction means you must wear corrective lenses, and the G restriction limits you to daylight hours only.
The V code shows that the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration gave the driver a medical variance.

cards.q: What does an L restriction bar?
cards.a: Driving a commercial vehicle with air brakes.

cards.q: What does a Z restriction bar?
cards.a: Driving a commercial vehicle with air brakes that are not fully equipped.

cards.q: What does an E restriction bar?
cards.a: Driving a CMV with a manual transmission.

cards.q: What does an O restriction bar?
cards.a: Driving a CMV with a tractor-trailer.

cards.q: What does a K restriction limit you to?
cards.a: Driving commercial vehicles inside the state only.

cards.q: How do you remove an E, L or O restriction?
cards.a: Get a qualifying permit and pass the skills tests.

exam.q: You take the skills test in a truck with hydraulic brakes. What goes on your licence?
choices: An L restriction barring air brakes
exam.why: Testing in a vehicle without air brakes gives the L restriction, which bars air brakes.

exam.q: How is an L restriction removed?
choices: With a qualifying permit and passing the skills test
exam.why: An E, L or O restriction needs a qualifying permit and a passed skills test.

reading.p: A restriction is a letter or a number on the licence that limits what you may drive. These are the ones a Utah CDL can carry.

reading.h: The ones that matter most to you

numbers.what: no commercial vehicle with air brakes
no commercial vehicle with air brakes that are not fully equipped
no commercial motor vehicle with a manual transmission
no commercial motor vehicle with a tractor-trailer
commercial driving inside the state only

reading.note: To remove an E, L or O restriction you must get a qualifying permit and pass the skills tests. Utah does not permit modified skills tests.

ul: A: no restrictions. B: corrective lenses. C: mechanical aid. D: prosthetic aid.
F: outside rearview mirrors. G: daylight hours only. J: any other restriction the Division thinks necessary.
M and N: no passengers in a Class A bus, or in a Class A or B bus.
P: a school bus or passenger endorsement holder may carry no passengers.
V: the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration has given the driver a medical variance.

facts.text: To keep a hazardous materials (H) endorsement in Utah you must pass a Transportation Security Administration background check every five years, and a written exam at first issue and at renewal.
To keep a school bus (S) endorsement in Utah you must pass a written exam when you renew the licence.
The X endorsement is the tank vehicle and hazardous materials combination.

cards.q: How often must an H endorsement holder pass a TSA background check in Utah?
cards.a: Every five years.

cards.q: What does the X endorsement cover?
cards.a: Tank vehicles and hazardous materials together.

reading.p: These are the endorsements a Utah CDL can carry.

numbers.what: motorcycle
tank vehicles
passengers
double or triple trailers
hazardous materials and tank combination
taxi
hazardous materials
school bus

reading.h: Two that need more than one test

ul: H: you must pass a Transportation Security Administration background check every five years, and a written exam at first issue and at renewal.
S: you must pass a written exam when you renew the licence.

facts.text: Get your medical examiner's certificate from a physician on the National Registry.
If you do not qualify for a medical certificate, a Utah K restriction may let you drive a commercial vehicle inside Utah only.
You must give a new medical certificate when the one before it expires, and your provider must put it on the National Registry before you apply.
If you drive a commercial vehicle over 10,001 pounds that needs no CDL, you must carry a medical certificate, but you do not have to give it to the Driver License Division.

cards.q: Who can issue your medical examiner's certificate?
cards.a: A physician on the National Registry.

cards.q: Which weight makes a non-CDL commercial driver carry an MEC?
cards.a: Over 10,001 lb. It is carried, not filed with the Division.

cards.q: What may you get if you cannot qualify for an MEC?
cards.a: A Utah K restriction, for driving inside Utah only.

reading.p: Get your medical examiner's certificate from a registered physician on the National Registry. The list is at the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration website.

ul: File a valid certificate and the self-certification form for an original, a renewal, an upgrade or a state to state transfer.
File a new certificate when the one before it expires.
Your provider must put the certificate on the National Registry before you apply, because it is added to your record electronically.

reading.note: If you cannot qualify for a certificate, a Utah K restriction may let you drive a commercial motor vehicle inside Utah only.

reading.p: If you drive a commercial vehicle over 10,001 pounds that needs no CDL, you must carry a medical certificate, but you do not have to file it with the Driver License Division.

facts.text: A motor vehicle record shows every moving violation for the last three years.
A drug or alcohol offence stays on your motor vehicle record for ten years.
The items on a CDL motor vehicle record stay on it for at least 55 years.
A citation entered as a plea in abeyance still appears on your record, and it cannot be taken off once it is there.

cards.q: How far back do moving violations show on an MVR?
cards.a: Three years.

cards.q: How long does a drug or alcohol offence stay on an MVR?
cards.a: Ten years.

cards.q: How long do items stay on a CDL MVR?
cards.a: At least 55 years.

cards.q: Can a plea in abeyance be removed from your record?
cards.a: No. It appears and stays.

exam.q: How long does a drug or alcohol offence stay on your motor vehicle record?
exam.why: Moving violations show for three years, but a drug or alcohol offence stays ten.

reading.p: A motor vehicle record, or MVR, can be obtained at any Driver License office. A CDL holder and an employer can get a CDL MVR, which holds more.

numbers.what: how far back moving violations show
how long a drug or alcohol offence stays
how long the items on a CDL MVR stay, at least

reading.p: A CDL MVR must include your driver history with convictions, pleas held in abeyance, disqualifications and other licensing actions, in any type of vehicle; your self-certification status; and your medical certification record.

reading.note: A citation entered as a plea in abeyance still appears on your record, and once it is there it cannot be removed.

reading.p: A CDL MVR is released only with a notarized release from the driver, or to the driver in person.

facts.text: You may not drive a commercial motor vehicle while you are disqualified, for any reason.

cards.q: May you drive a CMV while disqualified for any reason?
cards.a: No.

reading.p: You may not drive a commercial motor vehicle while you are disqualified, for any reason at all.

subsections.title: Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

facts.text: It is illegal to drive a CMV with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.04% or more.
By driving a CMV you are deemed to have consented to alcohol testing.

A first offence costs you your CDL for at least one year: a BAC of 0.04% or higher, driving under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance, refusing a test, leaving the scene of an accident, a felony with a CMV, driving on a suspended CDL, or causing a death by negligent driving.
The loss is at least three years if the offence happens while you drive a CMV placarded for hazardous materials.
A second offence costs you your CDL for life.
Using a CMV to commit a felony involving controlled substances costs you your CDL for life.
Any detectable alcohol under 0.04% puts you out of service for 24 hours.

cards.q: What BAC makes it illegal to drive a CMV?
cards.a: 0.04% or more.

cards.q: How long do you lose your CDL for a first alcohol offence?
cards.a: At least one year.

cards.q: How long for a first offence while placarded for hazmat?
cards.a: At least three years.

cards.q: What is the penalty for a second serious alcohol or drug offence?
cards.a: Loss of the CDL for life.

cards.q: What happens with any detectable alcohol under 0.04%?
cards.a: Out of service for 24 hours.

cards.q: What is the penalty for using a CMV in a controlled substance felony?
cards.a: Loss of the CDL for life.

cards.q: Does refusing a blood alcohol test carry a penalty?
cards.a: Yes. At least one year, the same as a first offence.

exam.q: You are driving a CMV placarded for hazardous materials and you are convicted of a first DUI. How long do you lose your CDL?
exam.why: A first offence is one year, but three years when the vehicle is placarded for hazmat.

exam.q: A test shows 0.02% BAC in a CMV driver. What happens?
choices: Nothing: it is under the limit
exam.why: Any detectable alcohol under 0.04% means 24 hours out of service.

exam.q: What is the penalty for refusing alcohol testing on a first offence?
exam.why: Refusing a test is treated like the other first offences: at least one year.

reading.p: These are the heaviest penalties in the manual, and the numbers are the answer to most of the questions about them.

numbers.what: the blood alcohol level at which driving a CMV is illegal
at least, for a first offence
at least, if the offence happens while placarded for hazmat
a second offence
out of service for any detectable alcohol under 0.04%

reading.h: What counts as a first offence

ul: A blood alcohol concentration of 0.04% or higher in a CMV.
Driving a CMV under the influence of alcohol, or of a controlled substance.
Refusing a blood alcohol test.
Leaving the scene of an accident involving a CMV.
Committing a felony with a CMV.
Driving a CMV while the CDL is suspended.
Causing a death through negligent driving of a CMV.

reading.note: By driving a CMV you are deemed to have consented to alcohol testing. Using a CMV to commit a felony involving controlled substances costs you the licence for life, first offence or not.

reading.p: In Utah it is also unlawful to use or possess powdered alcohol for human consumption.

facts.text: Excessive speeding, which is a serious traffic violation, means 15 mph or more above the posted limit.

Serious traffic violations also include reckless driving, improper or erratic lane changes, following too closely, a traffic offence in a CMV connected with a fatal accident, driving a CMV without a CDL or without it in your possession, and driving without the right class or endorsement.
Two serious traffic violations in a CMV within three years cost you your CDL for at least 60 days.
Three or more serious traffic violations in a CMV within three years cost you your CDL for at least 120 days.

cards.q: How far over the limit is excessive speeding?
cards.a: 15 mph or more above the posted limit.

cards.q: Penalty for two serious traffic violations in three years?
cards.a: At least 60 days.

cards.q: Penalty for three serious traffic violations in three years?
cards.a: At least 120 days.

exam.q: You get a third serious traffic violation inside three years. How long do you lose your CDL?
exam.why: Two in three years is 60 days; three or more is 120 days.

reading.p: A serious traffic violation is not a disqualification on its own. It is the second and third one inside three years that costs you the licence.

numbers.what: over the posted limit is excessive speeding
at least, for two serious violations in three years
at least, for three or more in three years

reading.h: What is a serious traffic violation

ul: Excessive speeding, 15 mph or more over the limit.
Reckless driving.
Improper or erratic lane changes.
Following a vehicle too closely.
A traffic offence in a CMV connected with a fatal accident.
Driving a CMV without a CDL, or without it in your possession.
Driving a CMV without the proper class of licence or endorsement.

facts.text: A first violation of an out-of-service order costs you your CDL for at least 90 days.
Two violations of an out-of-service order within ten years cost you your CDL for at least one year.
Three or more violations of an out-of-service order within ten years cost you your CDL for at least three years.

cards.q: Penalty for a first out-of-service order violation?
cards.a: At least 90 days.

cards.q: Penalty for two out-of-service violations in ten years?
cards.a: At least one year.

cards.q: Penalty for three out-of-service violations in ten years?
cards.a: At least three years.

exam.q: How long do you lose your CDL for a first violation of an out-of-service order?
exam.why: A first out-of-service violation is at least 90 days.

reading.p: An out-of-service order takes the vehicle or the driver off the road. Breaking one is treated severely.

numbers.what: at least, first violation
at least, two violations in ten years
at least, three or more violations in ten years

reading.note: Note the window: ten years, not three.

facts.text: A first railroad-highway grade crossing violation costs you your CDL for at least 60 days.
A second railroad crossing violation within three years costs you your CDL for at least 120 days.
A third railroad crossing violation within three years costs you your CDL for at least one year.

There are six railroad crossing offences, and they include not having enough space to drive all the way through the crossing without stopping, and not getting across because of too little undercarriage clearance.
A driver who need not always stop still must slow down, check that the tracks are clear, and stop before the crossing if they are not.

cards.q: Penalty for a first railroad crossing violation?
cards.a: At least 60 days.

cards.q: Penalty for a second railroad crossing violation in three years?
cards.a: At least 120 days.

cards.q: Penalty for a third railroad crossing violation in three years?
cards.a: At least one year.

cards.q: How many railroad crossing offences are listed?
cards.a: Six.

exam.q: You stop on a crossing because there was not enough room on the far side. What is this?
choices: No violation if you were moving
exam.why: Failing to have enough space to clear the crossing without stopping is one of the six offences.

reading.p: A railroad crossing violation has its own set of penalties, counted over three years.

numbers.what: at least, first violation
at least, second violation within three years
at least, third violation within three years

ul: A driver not always required to stop fails to stop before the crossing when the tracks are not clear.
A driver not always required to stop fails to slow down and check that the tracks are clear of a train.
A driver always required to stop fails to stop before driving onto the crossing.
Any driver fails to have enough space to drive all the way through the crossing without stopping.
Any driver fails to obey a traffic control device, or an enforcement official, at the crossing.
Any driver fails to get across because of too little undercarriage clearance.

facts.text: A hazardous materials endorsement needs your fingerprints and a background check.

You lose or are denied the hazmat endorsement if you are not a lawful permanent resident, give up your United States citizenship, are wanted or under indictment for certain felonies, were convicted of certain felonies, were found to lack mental capacity or were committed to a mental health facility, or the Transportation Security Administration judges you a security threat.

cards.q: What does a hazmat endorsement application need?
cards.a: Fingerprints and a background check.

reading.p: A hazardous materials endorsement needs your fingerprints and a background check.

reading.h: You are denied, or you lose it, if you

ul: Are not a lawful permanent resident of the United States.
Renounce your United States citizenship.
Are wanted or under indictment for certain felonies.
Have a conviction in a military or civilian court for certain felonies.
Have been found to lack mental capacity, or were involuntarily committed to a mental health facility.
Are judged a security threat by the Transportation Security Administration.

reading.p: Background check procedures differ by jurisdiction. Your licensing agency tells you what to do.

facts.text: If your right to drive your personal vehicle is revoked, cancelled or suspended for breaking traffic laws, other than parking, you lose your CDL driving privileges too.
If your personal licence is revoked, cancelled or suspended for alcohol, a controlled substance or a felony, you lose your CDL for one year.
A second such violation, in your personal vehicle or in a CMV, costs you your CDL for life.
You cannot get a hardship licence to drive a CMV while your personal licence is revoked, cancelled or suspended.

cards.q: Your car licence is suspended for DUI. What happens to your CDL?
cards.a: You lose it for one year.

cards.q: Can you get a hardship licence to drive a CMV?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: Second alcohol or felony violation, car or truck. What happens?
cards.a: You lose the CDL for life.

exam.q: You are convicted of DUI in your own car. What happens to your CDL?
choices: Nothing: it was not a CMV
You lose it for one year
exam.why: A personal-vehicle alcohol, drug or felony revocation costs the CDL for one year.

reading.p: What you do in your own car reaches your CDL. The Motor Carrier Safety Improvement Act of 1999 requires it.

ul: Lose your right to drive your personal vehicle for breaking traffic laws, other than parking, and you lose your CDL privileges too.
Lose it for alcohol, a controlled substance or a felony, and you lose your CDL for one year.
A second such violation, in your own vehicle or a CMV, costs you the CDL for life.

reading.note: You cannot get a hardship licence to drive a commercial motor vehicle while your personal licence is revoked, cancelled or suspended.

facts.text: You cannot hold more than one licence. A court can fine you up to $5,000 or put you in jail, and your home state keeps its licence while the others are returned.
You must tell your employer within 30 days of a conviction for any traffic violation except parking, whatever vehicle you were driving.
You must tell your motor vehicle licensing agency within 30 days if another jurisdiction convicts you of any traffic violation except parking.
You must tell your employer within two business days if your licence is suspended, revoked or cancelled, or if you are disqualified.
When you apply for a commercial driving job you must give the employer information on every driving job you held for the past ten years.
Nobody may drive a CMV without a CDL, and a court can fine you up to $5,000 or put you in jail for it.
With a hazardous materials endorsement you must tell the state that issued your CDL, and give up the endorsement, within 24 hours of a conviction or indictment for a disqualifying crime.
Your employer may not let you drive a CMV if you hold more than one licence or your CDL is suspended or revoked, and the employer can be fined up to $5,000 or jailed.
You may not hold a mobile telephone to make a voice call, and you may not dial one by pressing more than a single button, while driving.
You may not send or read text messages while driving.
You must wear the safety belt at all times while you drive a commercial motor vehicle. Without it you are four times more likely to be killed if you are thrown from the vehicle.
All states share one computer system for CDL information, and they check accident records so that no driver holds more than one CDL.

cards.q: How many licences may a CDL driver hold?
cards.a: One. The fine can reach $5,000 or jail.

cards.q: How soon must you tell your employer about a traffic conviction?
cards.a: Within 30 days, whatever vehicle you drove.

cards.q: How soon must you tell your employer that your licence is suspended?
cards.a: Within two business days.

cards.q: How many years of driving jobs must you give a new employer?
cards.a: Ten years.

cards.q: How soon must you surrender a hazmat endorsement after a disqualifying conviction?
cards.a: Within 24 hours.

cards.q: What are the mobile phone rules while driving a CMV?
cards.a: No holding it for a call, no dialling with more than one button, and no texting.

cards.q: How much more likely is death without a safety belt if you are thrown out?
cards.a: Four times.

exam.q: Your licence is suspended on Monday. By when must you tell your employer?
exam.why: A suspension, revocation, cancellation or disqualification goes to the employer within two business days.

exam.q: You are convicted of speeding in your own car. Must you tell your employer?
choices: No: it was not a CMV
exam.why: Any traffic conviction except parking goes to the employer within 30 days, whatever the vehicle.

exam.q: How many years of driving jobs must you report when you apply for a commercial driving job?
exam.why: You must give information on all driving jobs for the past ten years.

reading.p: These rules apply to drivers of commercial motor vehicles in every state. The deadlines are the part the test asks about.

facts.text: A CDL vehicle in interstate commerce must, with few exceptions, be registered under the International Registration Plan and the International Fuel Tax Agreement.
The two programmes cover the 48 adjoining United States and 10 Canadian provinces.
Under the plan a registrant must keep accurate distance records and make them available for review.

cards.q: Which two programmes must an interstate CDL vehicle be registered under?
cards.a: The International Registration Plan (IRP) and the International Fuel Tax Agreement (IFTA).

cards.q: How far do IRP and IFTA reach?
cards.a: The 48 adjoining states and 10 Canadian provinces.

reading.p: If you drive a CDL required vehicle in interstate commerce, the vehicle must, with few exceptions, be registered under two programmes: the International Registration Plan and the International Fuel Tax Agreement.
They share vehicle licence fees and motor fuel taxes fairly between the places you drive through, across the 48 adjoining United States and 10 Canadian provinces.

ul: Apply for registration with the base jurisdiction.
Provide the proper documents and pay the fees.
Display the registration credentials properly.
Keep accurate distance records, and make them available for review.
